name: Apology Craft
description: Two contestants face the same scenario — they've done something bad and need to make it right. Each round they draft an apology. The AI jury picks the apology most likely to actually mend the relationship: genuine ownership, concrete acknowledgment of harm, credible plan to prevent recurrence. Powered by the judged-contest engine (scenario: apology_craft).

phases.name: contest
phases.description: Contestants draft apologies in turn. Judges score sincerity, accountability, plan.

properties.name: wit
properties.description: Emotional intelligence — reading what the harmed party actually needs

properties.name: composure
properties.description: Holding accountability without collapsing into self-pity

properties.name: is_winner
properties.description: True after the jury declares them the winner.

entity_types.name: Judge
entity_types.description: A panel judge scoring the apology.

properties.name: harshness
properties.description: How aggressively they sniff out weasel words

properties.name: voted_for
properties.description: Contestant entity_id this judge voted for.

actions.name: make_argument
actions.description: Deliver your apology draft for this round. REQUIRED parameter `text`: the actual apology you'd say to the harmed party — first-person, direct, no hedging. Strong apologies (1) NAME the harm specifically, (2) take OWNERSHIP without 'if' or 'but', (3) acknowledge the impact on the other person, (4) propose a CONCRETE change going forward. Avoid 'I'm sorry IF you felt…', 'I'm sorry BUT…', 'mistakes were made'. Each round you can refine, respond to the other contestant's draft, or push your apology further.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Your apology draft for this round.

actions.name: cast_vote
actions.description: Cast your single vote for the contestant whose apology you'd actually accept. REQUIRED parameter `winner`: the entity_id of the contestant.

personas.persona_text: Reflective communicator. You take time to understand the harm before drafting. Your apologies are grounded, specific, and self-aware — no performative grovel.
goals: Win the jury's vote by crafting an apology that would actually be accepted.

personas.persona_text: Direct and concrete. You skip the soft preamble and go straight to ownership + plan. The harmed party knows exactly what you did and exactly what changes next.
goals: Win the jury's vote by crafting an apology that would actually be accepted.

personas.persona_text: Sincerity-first judge. Sniffs out 'I'm sorry IF' / 'I'm sorry BUT' / passive voice. Rewards apologies that genuinely OWN the harm in plain language.
goals: Cast a fair vote based on accountability and sincerity.

personas.persona_text: Plan-of-action judge. An apology without a credible 'here's what changes' is just emotion. You reward concrete, time-bound commitments.
goals: Cast a fair vote weighted toward demonstrated repair plan.

personas.persona_text: Empathy reader. You weigh whether the apology speaks to what the OTHER person actually needs to hear, not what the apologizer wants to say. Theory of mind matters.
goals: Cast a fair vote weighted toward emotional intelligence.

runtime_parameters.name: sample_size
runtime_parameters.label: Total Contestants
runtime_parameters.description: Apology craft is strictly 1v1 — two contestants, plus the AI jury.

runtime_parameters.name: domain.judged_contest.topic
runtime_parameters.label: Scenario (the harm)
runtime_parameters.default: You missed your best friend's wedding to take a work call. They haven't spoken to you in three weeks.
runtime_parameters.description: The scenario both contestants are apologizing for. Be specific about the harm.
presets: You missed your best friend's wedding to take a work call. They haven't spoken to you in three weeks.
You forgot your partner's birthday for the second year in a row.
You shipped a feature that broke production for a major customer; you ignored the QA report.
You told a story at a dinner party that revealed a friend's secret without their permission.
You took credit for a coworker's idea in a meeting with leadership.
You cancelled on your sibling's recital — again — and they overheard you say it was 'no big deal'.
You promised to call your aging parent every weekend and haven't called in two months.
You sent an angry text to a friend at 2am that you regretted by morning.

runtime_parameters.name: domain.judged_contest.contest_rounds

runtime_parameters.description: How many drafting rounds before the jury votes. Odd-only — one contestant always gets the closing draft. More rounds = more opportunity to refine.

runtime_parameters.name: domain.judged_contest.jury_size
